A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VideoFusion and M3SVD, with readable text, equations, tables and figures that support reliable matching. Both contain 11 pages and end with references; neither includes an appendix or embedded supplementary material. Referenced external supplements cannot be assessed.

before.justification: v2 reports original fusion experiments on M3SVD and HDO, component and loss ablations, computational measurements, and tracking examples in Section 5.

after.justification: v3 reports original fusion experiments, temporal-consistency measurements, ablations, computational measurements, and tracking examples in Section 5.

M1.justification: The same CmDRM, CMGF, BiCAM, modality-unmixing decoders and five-term training objective remain in v2 Section 3 and v3 Section 4. Multi-head attention and boundary-frame replication are newly specified, but the PDFs do not establish a changed algorithm. Diagram corrections align with the retained equations.

E1.justification: Both train on M3SVD, evaluate degraded fusion on M3SVD and HDO and normal fusion on M3SVD, and retain the M3SVD tracking demonstration. M3SVD still contains 220 video pairs and 153,797 frames across 100 scenes. Registration is newly mentioned as a dataset application, not evaluated as a new task.

E2.justification: Tables 2-4 and the corresponding visual comparisons replace DDBF and Text-IF with GIFNet and TemCoCo. The other seven fusion comparators and MDIVDNet/DSTNet preprocessing remain. Introducing a temporally modeling video-fusion competitor substantially changes the central comparison. UniVF is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: flowD replaces spatial frequency throughout the comparison and ablation tables, introducing direct quantitative temporal-coherence evaluation. Section 5.1 changes the previously unqualified T=7 setting to T=7 for training and T=25 for testing. The reported registration pipeline also adds XCP-Match alongside ReDFeat and MINIMA. These documented protocol revisions do not establish whether experiments were rerun or data regenerated.

E4.justification: The same seven component/loss ablations remain, but Table 5 adds flowD evidence about their temporal effects: 3.294 for the full model, 4.747 without BiCAM and 6.056 without the variational loss. Temporal and tracking comparisons are revised, while the ablation configurations and convergence analysis remain substantially unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both report point estimates and temporal/training trajectories; the revised scores do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Comparison and ablation scores change extensively, alongside added GIFNet, TemCoCo and flowD entries and removed DDBF, Text-IF and SF entries. Table 2 changes VideoFusion's M3SVD MI from 4.027 to 4.008 and HDO MI from 2.927 to 2.682. Table 4 changes DDFM runtime from 3.534 to 34.502 seconds. Revised settings prevent interpreting these as controlled before-and-after performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(13) retain the attention constructions, temporal-variation hypothesis and loss definitions. The multiplication-symbol change in Equation (5) does not introduce new mathematical reasoning. Boundary replication adds implementation detail; no new theorem, proof or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: v3 removes restoration from the title and advertised network contribution, removes the degraded-input qualifier from the abstract, and explicitly adds registration to the dataset's stated applications. This modestly changes the advertised scope; restoration outputs and the central dataset and temporal-fusion claims remain.

C2.justification: Discussion of DDBF/Text-IF failures is replaced by interpretations of GIFNet and TemCoCo, including attributing TemCoCo's blur to aggregation/restoration limitations. v3 interprets flowD as evidence for temporal modeling and adds arguments about DCN instability and optical-flow generalization. It also removes the static-background justification for using one homography per video.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project/M3SVD access link, specifies multi-head cross-attention and replication of boundary frames, explains the training-window memory constraint, and lists XCP-Match in dataset registration. Optimizer, epochs, loss weights, channel sizes and hardware remain documented as before. The link supplies access information without establishing external availability.

R1.justification: The Video Restoration discussion is replaced by a dedicated Video Fusion subsection covering RCVS, saPIDFuse, DFTP and concurrent TemCoCo/UniVF, positioning attention against handcrafted features, DCN and optical flow. References also add newer fusion methods and metric sources while removing several restoration works. This substantially revises research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method overview and experimental discussion undergo extensive rewriting. The dataset section moves before methodology, and related work becomes numbered Image Fusion and Video Fusion subsections. The title, affiliations, author ordering and terminology also change, producing a substantial narrative revision.

P2.justification: The architecture diagram moves from Figure 2 to Figure 4 and revises temporal labels, repetition annotations and operator symbols. Calibration and dataset illustrations are relocated, and the dataset gallery is reformatted. Figures 1 and 5-8 replace comparator panels or plots; Tables 2, 3 and 5 reorganize metric columns around flowD. These are broad visual changes.

improvement.justification: flowD measurements and the TemCoCo comparison provide more direct evidence for the central temporal-consistency claim than v2's comparisons and trajectory visualizations alone. Boundary handling, testing-window disclosure and project access information also improve reproducibility. These benefits are tempered by removing DDBF/Text-IF and SF comparisons and by unexplained revisions to many shared scores and runtimes, supporting a limited net improvement.
